summary: Iran war-driven energy inflation has markets repricing Fed policy under incoming chair Kevin Warsh, with traders now pricing nearly a two-thirds chance of a rate hike by December. That has hammered long-duration bonds, keeping real rates elevated and gold under pressure despite equity greed. U.S.-Iran peace talks remain stalled, with oil above $106, sustaining the inflation overhang across all asset classes.
tweet: Iran talks deadlocked, oil above $106, and a rate-hike bet under new Fed chair Warsh is punishing bonds and gold while stocks hold greed on earnings momentum.
